# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, wget, and certificates
# This is done in a single RUN command to reduce layer count.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /build

# Build and install all dependencies (Metis, Hypre, MFEM) and the application (Laghos) from source
# This is a single, long RUN command to keep the image layers to a minimum, as per best practices
# without using a multi-stage build.
RUN \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Metis 4.0.3 ---
    #
    echo "Building METIS..." && \
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    # The library is in the source root, but the header is in the 'Lib' subdirectory.
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build and Install Hypre 2.28.0 ---
    #
    echo "Building HYPRE..." && \
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    # Configure with MPI compilers and specified flags
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: The HYPRE 'make install' is incomplete. Copy headers and the static library manually.
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    echo "Building MFEM..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    git checkout v4.7 && \
    # Build the parallel version, pointing to the previously installed dependencies
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos ---
    #
    echo "Building Laghos..." && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    # Build the application, pointing to the MFEM source directory
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem && \
    # Copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cd ..

# Set the final working directory for the application runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the required data files from the Laghos source into the runtime WORKDIR,
# clean up the build directory to reduce image size, and update the linker cache.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/data/* . \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && ldconfig

# The entrypoint/command would be set at runtime, e.g., using 'mpirun -np 4 laghos ...'

updates.reason: The initial run on a 64-core ARM instance provides a strong baseline. This attempt switches to a high-performance 48 vCPU x86 instance (c7a.12xlarge) and maps tasks to its 24 physical cores. This strategy aims to improve performance by avoiding SMT/hyper-threading contention, which can be detrimental for CPU- and memory-bound HPC workloads.

The initial run on the ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance with 64 tasks achieved the highest performance (127.9). The subsequent attempt on a c7a.12xlarge x86 instance with 24 tasks (matching physical cores) yielded a lower score (124.5). This indicates that for this specific workload, either the higher core count or the Graviton3 architecture provides a significant advantage over the tested x86 configurations. Further tuning of x86 instances is unlikely to surpass the initial result. Therefore, the optimal configuration found is the first one.
